title: Pool check and pool-row item checks match answer regexes as agent_bench scores them, not with re.I
goal: bench_pool exposes the match agent_bench uses to score an answer (re.search with no flags today) and pool check and stale_picks use it, so a regex that fails at scoring, such as a cmpivot timeout regex without (?i) against 'Ten minutes', fails pool check, and item checks over pool rows call it instead of compiling with re.I (SP-honlhzdc: BG-v3fcyl3c's and BG-qnq3pjd2's checks passed with re.I; BG-tkgpxdva)

run:
import sys, tempfile, os, json
sys.path.insert(0, "_tools")
import bench_pool as bp
home = tempfile.mkdtemp()
os.makedirs(os.path.join(home, os.path.dirname(bp.EVAL_FILE)))
with open(os.path.join(home, bp.EVAL_FILE), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
    f.write("id,question,expect_paths,expect_answer,x\nq1,what,a.md,good,\n")
bp.fact_for = lambda home, case: ("kb/public/a.md", 5, "The timeout is Ten minutes long.")
def warned(rx):
    rows = [dict(id="P1", kind="fact", source="lookup_eval.csv:q1", checks=json.dumps([rx]))]
    return any("no check matches" in w for w in bp.stale_picks(rows, home=home))
miss, hit = warned("ten minutes"), warned("(?i)ten minutes")
print("case-sensitive miss warned:", miss, "(?i) warned:", hit, file=sys.stderr)
sys.exit(0 if miss and not hit else 1)
